correctness.rationale: For any proper coloring the outer neighborhoods are cliques and only the hub can fail PCF, so the success event equals X>=1 for singleton colors among r=q-1 colors. Conditional on the hub color, clique blocks are independent uniform injections. The exact coefficient identity is inclusion-exclusion over singleton events, independently matched to 423,262 direct assignments. For j target colors, uniformly bounded clique sizes give P(all singleton)=(S/r)^j exp(-jS/r)(1+o(1)); multi-target same-block events are O(M/S) relative and sum_i O(1/r²)=O(S/r²)=o(1). Thus E(X)_j~S^j exp(-jS/r)->exp(-jc), for all fixed j, and Poisson convergence follows by factorial moments. Independent tests of 21 more proper-color counts, 24 minimum-palette instances and selected moments passed. Finite testing is supporting, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Identifies a sharp, nondegenerate probability window for a natural graph-coloring witness property when the palette scales with graph order. The Poisson parameter and limiting success probability are universal across arbitrary heterogeneous bounded-size clique blocks, requiring new uniform estimates for dependent within-clique color draws. This quantifies abundance of PCF colorings beyond the pre-existing chromatic-number threshold and supports meaningful probabilistic analysis of one-cut-vertex block graphs; not merely an exact finite table or trivial relabeling.
